status: Two source-fit original action-plan designs reuse unchanged civic-goal and local-governance claims. They specify appropriate government and citizen actions, including a Nation government, without claiming plans were implemented or learners passed them.

food-access.provider: Nipissing First Nation, Food Bank/Social Services
food-access.use: Actual programme provides groceries to community members in need, with staff coordination and documented donation/fundraising/volunteer roles.
food-access.limits: The page mixes older and changed delivery details; those details, eligibility, hours, individual client information and current volunteering enrolment are not teaching instructions. The existence of a service does not mean every Nation member is in need or that it has eliminated food insecurity.

government-role.use: Previously verified complete municipal/FN/Métis entity and authority/service repertoire; department implementation is distinguished from governing-body authority.

fishery-response.use: Actual dated Nation/provincial responsibilities, measures and effect/uncertainty limits.

fishery-inquiry.use: Actual Nation and provincial sources, correct effort/result distinction and partial-recovery evidence.

whole-civic-claim.use: Retain the completed collective-action case, shared goal/values and original campaign-plan operation; no mastery inferred from the new links.

social-plan.issue: Food access for community members whom the actual programme supports; no inference about every person or family.
social-plan.goal: A bounded source-informed proposal to support clear service information and appropriately coordinated community contributions.

actors.body: Nipissing First Nation programme/Social Services staff

actionSteps.action: Propose that programme staff review clear, accessible public information and coordinate any currently suitable support needs with authorised community partners, using existing programme roles rather than inventing a new entitlement or budget decision.
actionSteps.purpose: Help appropriate participants find accurate information and keep support aligned with the programme’s stated needs.

actionSteps.action: Plan a clearly simulated awareness or support campaign based on a supplied, explicitly fictional approved-needs brief, choosing a suitable poster/letter/collection-plan method and explaining the shared goal, roles and next checks. No actual collection or claim that the Nation requested a school campaign is made.
actionSteps.purpose: Explain how citizens could contribute appropriately rather than replace government/service responsibilities or presume what a community wants.

actions: State the selected issue, a bounded intended improvement and whom the plan is for, using the verified source facts. Separate actual programme/role facts from the learner’s proposed future actions. Do not invent a failure or an entire community’s poverty, opinion or needs.

Generate at least two suitable citizen-action methods, consider likely consequences/limits, choose one and explain its fit to the shared goal. Specify a feasible sequence, who does what and what information/resources must be checked. The campaign plan is original work, not only a list of charitable or environmental words.

Include the explicit government and citizen action steps below, explain why each actor is appropriate and how the actions work together. Retain the independent whole local-governance checks from the original guide and complete civic-goal/campaign operation from the earlier dossier; a new case does not silently replace either claim.

Identify a modest way to check implementation/progress and what cannot be inferred from it. A completed poster, donation total or published update is not proof that food insecurity or a fish population problem has been solved.

Use a changed supplied social/environmental issue to justify actor/method choices rather than send the same petition or assign every issue to one generic government. Plans are assessed as designs; no real donation, enrolment, external message, political agreement or private household data is required.
social-plan.positive: Creates a specific plan with appropriate Nation/government and citizen steps, justified methods and a realistic bounded goal based on actual service facts.
nearMiss: Lists only citizen donations and no government/service action.
Assigns the programme to a nearby city without authority evidence or assumes every Nation member needs it.
Invents eligibility/delivery advice or claims a campaign would end all food insecurity.

environment-plan.issue: The documented stressed fishery and continuing recovery/management concern; source periods and uncertainty remain explicit.
environment-plan.goal: A bounded proposal supporting coordinated monitoring and accurate public understanding of the relevant stewardship information.

actors.body: Nipissing First Nation governing/programme authorities in the dated sources
Ontario ministry partner as named in the dated sources

actionSteps.action: Propose continuing appropriately coordinated assessment/communication within the documented Nation role, with experts setting actual fishery measures rather than the learner inventing new quotas or legal directions.
actionSteps.purpose: Support evidence-informed stewardship while retaining distinct Nation authority and the actual period/role limits.

actionSteps.action: Specify the corresponding provincial monitoring/management and public-information role from the source packet, including accurate dates and coordination with the Nation rather than substituting one government for the other.
actionSteps.purpose: Identify what the responsible government could contribute to the selected issue, without asserting an unverified agreement renewal or present entitlement.

actionSteps.action: Plan an original source-attributed awareness activity that explains the recovery concern and how to find current official information, rejecting the old inconsistent closure notice and the false net-count→fish-population inference. Choose and justify a suitable campaign method and division of roles.
actionSteps.purpose: Help public understanding without pretending a poster is itself a measured ecological recovery or asking a child to fish/sample/enforce rules.

limits: Government/citizen roles are explicit in both plans; the optional Native Languages programme exclusion does not remove these mandatory Indigenous-government source duties.
